body:
WHAT
When a session starts (boot, /clear, /resume) the `session_started` event carries the addon roster (name, description, builtin flag) and a `commands` list where every addon appears as `/<name>` with args `[args]` and its description, next to the built-in slash commands. The frontend's slash palette is built from this list, so addons show up without extra wiring.

WHY
The palette is never derived by the frontend; if the engine did not send addons in the registry, a user could not discover or tab-complete them.

WHERE
engine/core/src/runtime/engine.ts — Engine.announceSession() (`commands: [...SLASH_COMMANDS…, ...this.addonCommands()]`, `addons: this.addonSummaries()`), Engine.addonCommands(), Engine.addonSummaries(), Engine.emitAddonsUpdated() (same list after install). Roster source: engine/core/src/agent/addons.ts — loadAddons(), Addon.source used for the builtin flag.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. Booting an Engine with addons [{name:'foo', description:'D', source:'workspace'…}] emits session_started whose addons array contains {name:'foo', description:'D', builtin:false}.
2. The same session_started commands array contains an entry with cmd '/foo', args '[args]', desc 'D', and still contains every built-in such as '/help' and '/addons'.
3. The built-in magentron appears in session_started.addons with builtin:true.
4. After `/clear` the new session_started carries the same roster and `/foo` command again.
5. With no addons, session_started.addons is [] and commands equals exactly the built-in SLASH_COMMANDS list.
